It is a matter of profound spiritual gravity to sit with the “unsearchable riches” of Christ while witnessing a world where many “shave off the edges” of the truth to find “diplomatic relations” with a culture that “mocks, vilifies, and censures” the Scriptures, and I must ask you with a gentle heart: why do you ask after the nature of genuine Christian assurance in this digital hour? [1, 13, 28, 1503, 1605, Conversation History]. Are you perhaps feeling “overwhelmed and desperate” because your “heart is deceitfully wicked above all things, and desperately wicked; who can know it?” (Jeremiah 17:9), or are you seeking the “settled certainty” that “nothing... shall be able to separate us from the love of God which is in Christ Jesus our Lord” (Romans 8:38–39)? [335, 1409, 1429, 1431, 1462, 1605, Conversation History]. In a day when many offer “spiritual placebos,” “cliches,” or “cleverly devised myths,” we must return to the “external Word” to see how the Lord personally governs our confidence by promising that “He who has begun a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ” (Philippians 1:6) [1, 41, 319, 581, 913, 1503, Conversation History].

The Reformed tradition teaches that “God personally and exhaustively pervades and sustains and governs every aspect of His creation,” and therefore, your assurance is not an “administrative anomaly” based on your feelings but a “sovereign, gracious gift” rooted in the “decree from God” who “declares the end from the beginning” (Isaiah 46:10) [15, 68, 193, 1143, 1397, 1532, 1720, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 1: The Legal Ground of Assurance (Justification)**

**Verse**
“Therefore, having been justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom also we have access by faith into this grace in which we stand, and rejoice in hope of the glory of God” (Romans 5:1–2). [284, 1104, 1114, 1191, 1332, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Scriptures teach that assurance begins with a “past-tense, already-completed reality” where God, as the “eternal judge,” has issued a “forensic decree” that we are “pardoned, justified, and righteous” in His Son [73, 284, 286, Conversation History]. Our confidence is not a “one-time flu shot” or a “magic formula” we repeated, but it is grounded in the “finished work” of the One who was “delivered up because of our offenses, and was raised because of our justification” (Romans 4:25) [24, 136, 142, 322, 1445, Conversation History]. Because “He made Him who knew no sin to be sin for us, that we might become the righteousness of God in Him,” we can have a “settled confidence” that the debt is paid and “there is therefore now no condemnation to those who are in Christ Jesus” (2 Corinthians 5:21; Romans 8:1) [73, 251, 922, 928, 1326, 1429, 1507, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “not look for some other fountain of knowledge” in your own performance to find peace, for “if you are going to boast, boast in this, that you know and understand Me” (Jeremiah 9:24) [51, 123, 907, 1406, 1503, Conversation History]. Recognize that “your life is not your own” because “you were bought at a price,” and your “sole objective” is to rest in the truth that “not one human sinner or demonic power will ever succeed in his rebellion” against the King who has secured you (1 Corinthians 6:19–20) [11, 12, 15, 68, 101, 249, 1138, 1143, 1262, 1406, 1532, 1670, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Lineage vs. Grace**
In the ancient **Jewish context**, many believed their “lineage, their circumcision, their ceremonies, and their traditions” were what qualified them for the kingdom [262, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** this by showing that “he is not a Jew who is one outwardly... but he is a Jew who is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the Spirit,” for “the law and the prophets were until John,” and now the kingdom is preached through Christ (Romans 2:28–29; Luke 16:16) [254, 301, 1299, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 2: The Spirit’s Internal Witness (Adoption)**

**Verse**
“For you did not receive the spirit of bondage again to fear, but you received the Spirit of adoption by whom we cry out, ‘Abba, Father.’ The Spirit Himself bears witness with our spirit that we are children of God, and if children, then heirs—heirs of God and joint heirs with Christ” (Romans 8:15–17). [435, 708, 1008, 1195, 1197, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed faith—echoed by **John MacArthur**—asserts that “true Christianity” includes a “Spirit-wrought confidence” that “casts out the spirit of fear that comes from slavery to sin” [443, 1429, Conversation History]. This assurance is an “intimate endearment” where we address the “omnipotent Creator” as “Papa,” knowing that “as many as are led by the Spirit of God, these are sons of God” (Romans 8:14) [436, 709, 710, 1008, Conversation History]. The Holy Spirit acts as a “seal,” which is “an official mark of identification” conveying “authenticity, security, ownership, and authority” until the day we enter “eternal glory” (Ephesians 1:13) [721, 722, 1217, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Trade in your worry for trust,” for your “Heavenly Father knows that you need all these things” and He “will never leave you nor forsake you” (Matthew 6:32; Hebrews 13:5) [38, 69, 86, 94, 201, 407, 1013, 1266, 1408, 1515, Conversation History]. You must “discipline your body” to “pray without ceasing,” recognizing that “God’s purpose in prayer is not for us to inform or persuade Him... but to open sincere and continual lines of communication” with our “loving, beneficent Father” (1 Thessalonians 5:17) [10, 14, 31, 79, 116, 1194, 1406, 1709, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Bondage vs. Liberty**
Under the **Mosaic Law**, those who failed to “observe all these commandments” were under a “curse,” leading to a “spirit of bondage again to fear” (Deuteronomy 28:15) [977, 997, 1271, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our posture, revealing that “now we have been delivered from the law... so that we should serve in the newness of the Spirit,” for “where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty” (Romans 7:6; 2 Corinthians 3:17) [996, 1272, 1273, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 3: The Evidence of Fruit (Sanctification)**

**Verse**
“Now by this we know that we know Him, if we keep His commandments. He who says, ‘I know Him,’ and does not keep His commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him. But whoever keeps His word, truly the love of God is perfected in him. By this we know that we are in Him” (1 John 2:3–5). [381, 1087, 1104, 1134, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The sources teach that while “salvation is by grace alone,” it “inevitably produces 'fruit in keeping with repentance' ” because “a tree is known by its fruit” (Matthew 3:8; 12:33) [240, 328, 405, 473, Conversation History]. The Reformed tradition—echoed by **Paul Washer**—notes that “assurance is not a magic formula” but is strengthened as we “walk in the Spirit” and see the “fruit of the Spirit” manifest as “love, joy, peace, longsuffering, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control” (Galatians 5:22–23) [322, 500, 701, 740, 931, Conversation History]. Those who “persist in patterns of disobedience” while claiming to be saved are “slaves of corruption” who “lie and do not practice the truth” (1 John 1:6; 2 Peter 2:19) [382, 406, 449, 1201, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “examine yourself as to whether you are in the faith,” not by comparing yourself to others but by asking if “your heart is wrought upon” by the Word of God (2 Corinthians 13:5) [25, 319, 1103, 1201, 1406, Conversation History]. Recognize that “he who trusts in his own heart is a fool,” and you must instead “tremble at My word,” allowing it to “dominate your attitudes and actions” (Proverbs 28:26; Isaiah 66:2) [11, 42, 87, 178, 251, 744, 745, 851, 1134, 1313, 1406, 1445, 1503, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Ritual vs. Obedience**
In the ancient **context**, the Pharisees “neglected the weightier matters of the law: justice and mercy and faith” while obsessing over “ritualized ceremonies” and “legal minutiae” (Matthew 23:23) [8, 14, 271, 1091, 1352, Conversation History]. Jesus **upholds** a higher standard, teaching that “in vain they worship Me, teaching as doctrines the commandments of men,” and instead calls us to the “perfect law of liberty” where “true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth” (Matthew 15:9; John 4:23; James 1:25) [1126, 1276, 1316, 1431, 1503, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 4: Anchoring Amid Failure and Accusation (The Keeping Power)**

**Verse**
“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness” (1 John 1:9). [74, 229, 273, 1152, 1349, Conversation History]. “Who shall bring a charge against God’s elect? It is God who justifies. Who is he who condemns? It is Christ who died, and furthermore is also risen, who is even at the right hand of God, who also makes intercession for us” (Romans 8:33–34). [73, 1326, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
Scripture handles the “noise and tumult” of failures and the “accusations of conscience” by revealing that Christ is our “Advocate with the Father,” who “always lives to make intercession” for us (1 John 2:1; Hebrews 7:25) [13, 20, 1179, 1503, 1605, Conversation History]. The Reformed tradition—upheld by **Voddie Baucham**—teaches that “God is able to keep you from stumbling,” and therefore “no one, human or satanic, can permanently lay any charge against us” because the “Judge of all the earth” has declared us pardoned (Jude 24; Genesis 18:25) [73, 937, 938, 1143, 1459, 1532, 1720, Conversation History]. Even when “our heart condemns us, God is greater than our heart, and knows all things,” ensuring that His “keeping power” preserves the “church militant” until the end (1 John 3:20) [893, 1362, 1404, 1459, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
When your “foot is slipping,” find “tranquility of soul” in the promise that “Your love, O LORD, supported me” (Psalm 94:18) [11, 24, 150, 201, 216, 1118, 1143, 1315, 1408, 1450, 1515, Conversation History]. “Wait for His Son from heaven,” knowing that “He who has begun a good work in you will complete it,” for “scars... don’t define us; our hope does” (1 Thessalonians 1:10; Philippians 1:6) [14, 24, 94, 109, 201, 252, 891, 900, 913, 1315, 1408, 1450, 1515, 1720, Conversation History].

***

**Final Reminder**
“Nevertheless the firm foundation of God stands, having this seal, ‘The Lord knows those who are His,’ and, ‘Everyone who names the name of the Lord is to abstain from wickedness’ ” (2 Timothy 2:19). [11, 87, 147, 176, 211, 222, 285, 300, 313, 324, 332, 335, 361, 402, 405, 413, 414, 444, 449, 591, 1138, 1407, 1441, 1450, Conversation History].

Pass or Fail? When we speak of a trial or test, we will either pass or fail. Thus every trial God allows can turn into a temptation. Long after Joseph’s brothers sold him into slavery in Egypt, he told them, “You meant evil against me, but God meant it for good” (Gen. 50:20). Every struggle and trial we experience is allowed by God to test us, to exercise our spiritual muscles, and to help us mature (cf. 1 Peter 5:10). But if you don’t commit the situation to God and stand in His strength, Satan will turn it into a temptation. He will entice your lusts and may draw you into sin.

Anxiety is, at its core, an inappropriate response in light of circumstances; it’s very different from the cares and concerns in life that cause people to attend to business in a responsible way. Stress and pressure, instead of being things to avoid, strengthen us to accomplish the challenges God sets before us in life. The apostle Paul wrote that apart from the unrelenting external pressures he had to face, such as persecution, hardship, and imprisonment, he also had daily upon him the internal pressure “of concern for all the churches” (2 Cor. 11:28). In spite of that, he had room in his heart to feel the anxiety of others, for he went on to write, “Who is weak without my being weak? Who is led into sin without my intense concern?” (v. 29). He wouldn’t have had it any other way, though. In fact, that kind of response to pressure was what Paul looked for in those who would serve with him. Note how he commended Timothy to the Philippian church: “I have no one else of kindred spirit who will genuinely be concerned for your welfare” (Phil. 2:20; cf. 1 Cor. 4:17).

Humility toward Others When Peter said to “clothe yourselves with humility toward one another” (1 Peter 5:5), he had a specific image in mind. He used a Greek term that means to tie something on oneself with a knot or a bow. It came to refer especially to a work apron. Slaves would put on aprons over their clothes to keep them clean, just as you might do before you start a messy chore. The word became a synonym for humble service.

In fact, clarifying the gospel was the most important and constant emphasis of my writing— from The Gospel According to Jesus, Ashamed of the Gospel, Hard to Believe, and The Truth War to countless sermons and articles through the years. But through all those efforts, a profound and comprehensive perspective, one that dominates the New Testament and is crucial to the gospel, escaped me and almost everyone else. It wasn’t until the spring of 2007, on an all-night flight to London while reading Slave of Christ by Murray J. Harris, that I realized there had been a centuries-long cover-up by English New Testament translators that had obscured a precious, powerful, and clarifying revelation by the Holy Spirit. Undoubtedly, the cover-up was not intentional—at least not initially. Yet its results have been dramatically serious.

As Paul explained to Timothy: The firm foundation of God stands, having this seal, “The Lord knows those who are His,” and, “Everyone who names the name of the Lord is to abstain from wickedness.” Now in a large house there are not only gold and silver vessels, but also vessels of wood and of earthenware, and some to honor and some to dishonor. Therefore, if anyone cleanses himself from these things, he will be a vessel for honor, sanctified, useful to the Master, prepared for every good work. Now flee from youthful lusts and pursue righteousness, faith, love and peace, with those who call on the Lord from a pure heart. (2 Tim. 2:19–22)

Not everyone who says to Me, “Lord, Lord,” will enter the kingdom of heaven, but he who does the will of My Father who is in heaven will enter. Many will say to Me on that day, “Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in Your name, and in Your name cast out demons, and in Your name perform many miracles?” And then I will declare to them, “I never knew you; DEPART FROM ME, YOU WHO PRACTICE LAWLESSNESS” (Matt. 7:21–23). Clearly, not all who claim to know the Lord actually do. Those who truly “belong to Christ Jesus have crucified the flesh with its passions and desires” (Gal. 5:24). Rather than walking in the flesh, they now “walk by the Spirit” (v. 25), being characterized by a growing desire to obey the Word of God.
